=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:`_project_trigger`, the `if stem.startswith("implement-plan ") and wanted.startswith(stem):` block | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When the trigger Routine name for a long slug is truncated at 60 chars with `…`, the stem is longer than `wanted` (because `wanted = f"implement-plan {slug}:"` is missing the kind suffix and the truncated chars), so `wanted.startswith(stem)` returns False and the first `name.startswith(wanted)` branch also fails (the truncated name is longer than wanted). This causes a true-positive miss. The function relies on the prompt-path check `f"/{slug}-plan.md" in trigger["prompt"]` to recover, but a Routine prompt that doesn't contain that exact path (e.g. an old safety net with the path rewritten) would then be missed.
  WHY: For any `/implement-plan-claude` slug whose Routine name is truncated, the requeue guard fails to recognise the matching trigger and proceeds to requeue, producing a duplicate trigger for a project whose existing safety net still has an active check-in. The prompt-path fallback is best-effort, not a guarantee.
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:`gh_api`, the `raise ReadError(...)` after a non-zero exit | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `ReadError` message only carries the last non-empty line of stderr/stdout and never includes the request path. When `decide()` catches it inside `_issue_open_unblocked` or `_recent_reclarify` and appends `f"{checker} ({slug}): {exc}`, the resulting `errors[]` line names the checker and slug but not the endpoint, so the next wake (or a human reading the JSON) cannot tell whether `/repos/{repo}/issues/{n}` or `/repos/{repo}/issues/{n}/comments` failed.
  WHY: With multiple candidates, repeated transient failures are hard to attribute to one endpoint; the script is fail-safe so this never blocks restarts, but on-call triage is unnecessarily blind.
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:`read_project_logs`, the per-branch `git show` loop and the `_git(["show", ...])` call | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The per-branch `git show` is run sequentially with a fixed 30-second timeout. A deeply nested or unusually slow `docs/implement-plan/<slug>.md` on a heavy remote could time out on the first wake after a branch was force-pushed with a large log; the wrapped `ReadError` is silently swallowed (`continue`) and that branch drops from the log candidates for the rest of the wake — and the matching checker is then missed by `_evaluate_requeue`.
  WHY: A successful subsequent wake retries the read (idempotent), so this only delays a restart by one cycle. The current code already logs nothing to `errors[]` when `git show` fails, which is inconsistent with the open-issue and comment reads (both of which surface failures).
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:`read_project_logs`, the `for branch in present:` loop | severity=NIT | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: One `git show` runs per present branch in series. With the typical 1-2 `claude/implement-plan-issue-*` project branches per repo this is trivial, but the script is structured to handle many (no cap on `list_project_branches`), and each `git show` is a cold fork + checkout.
  WHY: No wall-clock or API failure today. At the LOOKUP_CAP-aligned project-branch volume the script is designed for, the work is bounded.
